pos.personaBrief: Positional play is an in-possession philosophy built on superiority through passing, with Guardiola's Barcelona and City at 65-68% possession and a 15-pass rule; possession is also protection (Spielverlagerung, Hard Tackle).

pro.personaBrief: Patient build-up from the goalkeeper with centre-backs wide and a number six between lines (Coaches' Voice, Salida Lavolpiana); the 15-pass rule means no rushed attacks, but passes aim to break lines, not go sideways for nothing.

est.personaBrief: Players are assigned to zones with strict rules on lines and spacing (Coaches' Voice), wide forwards stay out wide to pin full-backs (StatsBomb), and the aim is spread staggering rather than rondo-like crowding.

lar.personaBrief: Uses the whole width (wide columns and half-spaces) to open up the centre, with wide forwards pinning full-backs and Xavi, Iniesta, Messi in the middle (Coaches' Voice, StatsBomb); crossing wingers are not the aim.

blo.personaBrief: Counter-pressing partners positional play and Barcelona defended high with a high line (Coaches' Voice, Hard Tackle, StatsBomb); staggered positioning gives counter-press structure, though attacks are built rather than rehearsed from high steals.

mar.personaBrief: Defending is mostly a consequence of the possession structure, with zonal positional roots and Lillo's zonal marking influence, though Guardiola accepted man-for-man matchups at the back (Spielverlagerung, El Grafico); zone leans.

pla.personaBrief: A fixed game model imposed everywhere: the coach arrives with the system and players must adapt, planning starts from the ball and own structure (Publico: always from the ball; Guardiola 'restrictive' with players).

res.personaBrief: Style and how you win matter as much as outcome: possession with purpose, the 'best, most distinctive' playing style, and refusal to retreat; Guardiola's sides keep attacking rather than parking.

sis.personaBrief: The system is the star: strict zone rules, committed to the system, everyone defends and counter-presses (Coaches' Voice), though Messi got freedom within it; the collective lifts ordinary players.

jog.personaBrief: Technique and decision-making in tight spaces are the base (Xavi, Iniesta, La Masia), with high running commitment for recovery (Coaches' Voice); duels and aerial play are not decisive.

bas.personaBrief: Lineage from Cruyff's La Masia redesign and the Xavi-Iniesta-Messi core (Guide to Football, Hard Tackle); development matters but veterans and signings also play under Guardiola.

lid.personaBrief: Coaches explain the purpose of every pass and are restrictive about positions (Publico, Training Ground Guru), with rules for all but Messi given freedom; authority on the model while communicating reasons.
